library_name: Market Pattern & Technical Indicator Reference Library
purpose: Expanded machine-readable research catalogue for chart formations, candlestick formations, technical indicators, market structure/liquidity concepts and quantitative research features.
scope_note: Broad multi-source catalogue; not literally every proprietary, regional, discretionary or renamed concept. Similar names can have conflicting definitions. Each non-canonical definition must remain versioned and be validated before use.

source_baseline.name: TA-Lib Functions Catalogue
source_baseline.use: Canonical list and reference implementations for indicators, volatility, volume, statistics, price transforms and CDL candlestick recognizers.

source_baseline.name: TA-Lib Candlestick Outputs
source_baseline.use: Candlestick output encoding and reminder that pattern detections do not themselves confirm a trade.

source_baseline.name: StockCharts ChartSchool – Chart Patterns
source_baseline.use: Classic chart pattern taxonomy, reversal/continuation groupings and limitations.

source_baseline.name: TradingView – All Chart Patterns
source_baseline.use: Cross-check of commonly automated classic chart formations.

source_baseline.name: CRAN talib vignette – Candlestick Pattern Recognition
source_baseline.use: 61 TA-Lib candle functions, adaptive body/shadow thresholds and lookback considerations.

global_rules: Pattern recognition output is not a trade recommendation or proof of predictive power.
Keep detection, confirmation, entry, exit and position sizing as separate layers.
Do not use unconfirmed pivots, future bars, or revised higher-timeframe candles (look-ahead bias).
Store exact rule version, parameters, data vendor, timeframe and instrument with each experiment.
Use corporate-action-adjusted prices for equities and preserve raw prices for execution simulation.
Never assume volume exists or is comparable across all assets/venues.
For harmonic, Elliott and Wyckoff methods, preserve alternative counts/events and confidence; do not force a single answer.
Benchmark every detected pattern against a simple baseline and random/time-shuffled controls.

standard_signal_contract.timestamp_rule: Timestamp must be the first time the signal was actually knowable, not the first pivot bar if later bars were required for confirmation.

research_guardrails: A catalogue item is a hypothesis/specification, not evidence of edge or permission to trade.
Keep detector, context filter, confirmation, entry, sizing, stop, exit and execution-cost models separate.
Every signal must store first_knowable_at, source bar timestamp, data version, code commit and full parameter JSON.
All pivots and higher-timeframe bars become available only after confirmation/close; never backdate.
Use point-in-time universes and corporate-action-adjusted data; avoid survivorship and delisting bias.
Use chronological train/validation/untouched test splits and nested walk-forward evaluation.
Track the number of strategy variants tried; use multiple-testing controls and deflated/adjusted performance statistics where appropriate.
Include brokerage, taxes/fees, spread, slippage, market impact, lot size, tick size, liquidity, circuits and realistic fills.
Report long/short separately, market/session regimes, instrument, timeframe and liquidity buckets.
Persist failed experiments; never silently discard weak or losing results.
Do not optimise on the final holdout. Re-open holdout only under a new dated research version.
Promotion to paper trading requires minimum trade count, stable out-of-sample results, robustness tests and operational checks.
